final_message:
I implemented `diffLines`, `renderDiff` and `diffStats` in `src/diff.ts`, and the three existing tests pass under `npm test`. I didn't add tests of my own, and I checked the tie-break rule only by hand on one small case.

`diffLines` builds a table of the longest common subsequence for every pair of suffixes of `a` and `b`. It then walks forward from the front as the README describes. Equal lines are kept. Otherwise it deletes the next line of `a` if the rest of `a` still has as many lines in common with `b` as before, and inserts the next line of `b` if not. The leftover lines are then deleted or inserted. The table takes memory proportional to the product of the two lengths.

The hand check was `["p","q"]` against `["q","p"]`, which the rule resolves to delete `p`, keep `q`, add `p`.
